CITY OF
  HUNTINGTON PARK

  Council Member  Council Member

All agenda items and reports are available for review in the City Clerk’s Office and
www.hpca.gov. Any writings or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding
any item on this agenda (other than writings legally exempt from public disclosure) will be
made available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk located at 6550 Miles
Avenue, Huntington Park, California 90255 during regular business hours, 7:00 a.m. to 5:30
p.m., Monday – Thursday, and at the City Hall Council Chambers during the meeting.

Any person who requires a disability-related modification or accommodation, including
auxiliary aids or services, in order to participate in the public meeting may request such
modification, accommodation, aid or service by contacting the City Clerk’s Office either in
person at 6550 Miles Avenue, Huntington Park, California or by telephone at (323) 584-6230.
Notification in advance of the meeting will enable the city to make reasonable arrangements
to ensure accessibility to this meeting.

PLEASE SILENCE ALL CELL PHONES AND OTHER ELECTRONIC EQUIPMENT WHILE
COUNCIL IS IN SESSION. Thank you.

PLEASE NOTE-The numerical order of items on this agenda is for convenience of reference.
Items may be taken out of order upon request of the Mayor or Members of the City Council.
Members of the City Council and the public are reminded that they must preserve order and
decorum throughout the Meeting. In that regard, Members of the City Council and the public
are advised that any delay or disruption in the proceedings or a refusal to obey the orders of
the City Council or the presiding officer constitutes a violation of these rules.
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING AGENDA
 October 13, 2026  Page 1 of 6
   •  The conduct of City Council meetings is governed by the portion of the California
  Government Code, commonly known as the "Brown Act" and by the Huntington Park
  City Council Meeting Rules of Procedure.

  •  The City Council meeting is for conducting the City's business, and members of the
  audience must obey the rules of decorum set forth by law. This means that each speaker
  will be permitted to speak for three minutes to address items that are listed on the City
  Council agenda or topics which are within the jurisdictional authority of the City.

  •  No profanity, personal attacks, booing, cheering, applauding or other conduct disruptive
  to the meeting will be permitted. Any person not adhering to the Rules of Procedure or
  conduct authorized by the Brown Act may be asked to leave the Council Chambers.

  •  All comments directed to the City Council or to any member of the City Council must be
  directed to the mayor (or Chairperson if Mayor is absent).

We ask that you please respect the business nature of this meeting and the order required for
the proceedings conducted in the Council Chambers.

PUBLIC COMMENT

For both open and closed sessions, each speaker will be limited to three minutes per Huntington
Park Municipal Code Section 2-1.207. Time limits may not be shared with other speakers and
may not accumulate from one period of public comment to another or from one meeting to
another. This is the only opportunity for public input except for scheduled public hearing
items.

All comments or queries should be addressed to the Council as a body and not to any specific
member thereof. Pursuant to Government Code Section 54954.2(a)(2), the Ralph M. Brown Act,
no action or discussion by the City Council shall be undertaken on any item not appearing on the
posted agenda, except to briefly provide information, ask for clarification, provide direction to
staff, or schedule a matter for a future meeting.

ADDITIONS/DELETIONS TO AGENDA
Items of business may be added to the agenda upon a motion adopted by a minimum two-thirds
of vote finding that there is a need to take immediate action and that the need for action came to
the attention of the City or Agency subsequent to the agenda being posted. Items may be deleted
from the agenda upon the request of staff or Council.

 IMPORTANT NOTICE

The City of Huntington Park shows replays of City Council Meetings on Local Access
Channel 3 and on the Internet at www.hpca.gov. NOTE: Your attendance at this public
meeting may result in the recording and broadcast of your image and/or voice.

limited to three minutes per Huntington Park Municipal Code Section 2-1.207. Time limits may not
be shared with other speakers and may not accumulate from one period of public comment to another
or from one meeting to another.

  CONSENT CALENDAR

All matters listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one
motion. There will be no separate discussion of these matters prior to the time the Council votes on
the motion unless members of the Council, staff, or the public request specific items to be discussed
and/or removed from the Consent Calendar for separate action.

CITY CLERK

1.  CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT CITY COUNCIL:

  Approve Minute(s) of the following City Council Meeting(s):

  1. Special City Council Meeting on September 22, 2026

  2. Regular City Council Meeting on September 22, 2026

2.  NOMINATION AND CONSIDERATION OF APPOINTMENT TO THE YOUTH
  COMMISSION AND THE PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT CITY COUNCIL

  1. Consideration, nomination and appointment of Isabella Y. Razo as a
  commissioner to fill a vacancy in the Youth Commission.

  2. Consideration, nomination and appointment of Marianna Tabares as a
  commissioner to fill a vacancy in the Parks and Recreation Commission.

FINANCE

3.  WARRANT REGISTERS

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT CITY COUNCIL:

  1. Approve Accounts Payable and Payroll Warrant(s) dated October 8, 2026

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING AGENDA
  October 13, 2026  Page 4 of 6
 PUBLIC WORKS

4.  CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL OF AMENDMENT NO. 2 TO THE
  CONSTRUCTION AGREEMENT WITH AZTECS TELECOM INC. TO UPDATE
  SPECIFIC UNIT PRICES FOR THE BROADBAND INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECT

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT THE CITY COUNCIL:

  1. Approve Amendment No. 2 to the Design-Build Construction Agreement with
  Aztecs Telecom Inc. to update specific unit prices that have experienced material
  cost increases since the project’s original pricing was established;

  2. Authorize the continued use of project contingency to absorb the cost impacts
  associated with the updated unit prices, consistent with CPUC Federal Funding
  Account (FFA) grant eligibility; and

  3. Authorize the City Manager to execute Amendment No. 2 and all related documents
  necessary to implement the updated unit pricing.

5.  CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL OF CHANGE ORDERS NO. 9–22 FOR THE
  EMERGENCY OPERATIONS CENTER (EOC) CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT WITH
  BEDROCK GROUP, INC.

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT THE CITY COUNCIL:

  1. Approve Change Orders No. 9 through 22 for the Emergency Operations Center
  (EOC) Project, Contract No. 2024-01, with Bedrock Group, Inc., in the combined
  amount of $829,987.77; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute all related documents.

6.  CONSIDERATION OF APPROVAL OF CONSTRUCTION CHANGE ORDERS 1-12
  FOR CIP 2025-03 CITY HALL RENOVATION PROJECT

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT THE CITY COUNCIL:

  1. Approve the construction change orders 1-12 for the construction of CIP 2025-03
  City Hall Renovation Project for the not-to-exceed amount of $528,491.07.

7.  CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL OF CHANGE ORDER NO. 3 TO THE
  PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH EN ENGINEERING FOR
  ADDITIONAL PERMIT FEE REIMBURSEMENTS AND ANTICIPATED PERMIT
  COSTS

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT THE CITY COUNCIL:

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING AGENDA
  October 13, 2026  Page 5 of 6
   1. Approve Change Order No. 3 to the Professional Services Agreement with EN
  Engineering (Entrust Solutions Group) for Project No. 2530541.01 – Huntington
  Park Fiber Permitting, increasing the contract amount by $452,313.20 for
  reimbursement of permit fees paid to third-party agencies;

  2. Authorize an additional appropriation of $110,000 to EN Engineering for anticipated
  future permit fees required by railroads, transportation agencies, and municipal
  jurisdictions as the fiber project advances; and

  3. Authorize the City Manager to execute the change order and all related documents.

  END OF CONSENT CALENDAR

  ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

CITY MANAGER

1.  INTRODUCTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 2026-XX, ADDING CHAPTER 11
  (HUNTINGTON PARK BROADBAND SYSTEM) TO TITLE VII (PUBLIC WORKS) OF
  THE HUNTINGTON PARK MUNICIPAL CODE TO ESTABLISH THE HUNTINGTON
  PARK MUNICIPAL BROADBAND SYSTEM AS A CITY-OWNED PUBLIC UTILITY

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT THE CITY COUNCIL:

  1. Waive full reading and introduce Ordinance No. 2026-XX, by title only, adding
  Chapter 11 (Huntington Park Broadband System) to Title VII (Public Works) of the
  Huntington Park Municipal Code;

  2. Find and determine that adoption of Ordinance No. 2026-XX is exempt from the
  California Environmental Quality Act (Pub. Res. Code § 21000 et seq.) (“CEQA”)
  pursuant to State CEQA Guidelines (Cal. Code Regs., tit. 14, § 15000 et seq.)
  Section 15061(b)(3);
  3. Schedule second reading and adoption of Ordinance No. 2026-XX for the October
  27, 2026 City Council meeting; and

  4. Take such additional, related action that may be desirable.

2.  INTRODUCTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 2026-XX AMENDING CHAPTER 5
  (PURCHASING) OF TITLE 2 (ADMINISTRATION) OF THE HUNTINGTON PARK
  MUNICIPAL CODE TO ESTABLISH CONTRACT INTEGRITY AND VENDOR
  ACCOUNTABILITY STANDARDS FOR THE PROCUREMENT AND AMENDMENT
  OF CITY CONTRACTS

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT THE CITY COUNCIL:

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING AGENDA
  October 13, 2026  Page 6 of 6
   1. Waive full reading and introduce Ordinance No. 2026-XX, by title only, amending
  Chapter 5 (Purchasing) of Title 2 (Administration) of the Huntington Park Municipal
  Code to establish contract integrity and vendor accountability standards for the
  procurement and amendment of City contracts;

  2. Find and determine that adoption of Ordinance No. 2026-XX is exempt from the
  California Environmental Quality Act (Pub. Res. Code § 21000 et seq.)(“CEQA”)
  pursuant to State CEQA Guidelines (Cal. Code Regs. Tit. 14, § 15000 et seq.)
  Section (b)(3);

  3. Schedule second reading and adoption of Ordinance No. 2026-XX for the October
  27, 2026 City Council meeting; and

  4. Take such additional, related action that may be desirable.

3.  CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL OF AN ORDINANCE AMENDING CHAPTER 5
  (PURCHASING) OF TITLE 2 (ADMINISTRATION) OF THE HUNTINGTON PARK
  MUNICIPAL CODE BY ADDING SECTIONS TO ESTABLISH FINANCIAL DUE
  DILIGENCE STANDARDS PRIOR TO ENTERING INTO CITY CONTRACTS AND
  AWARDING PUBLIC BENEFITS

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT THE CITY COUNCIL:

  1. Waive first reading and introduce Ordinance No. 2026-XX, amending Chapter 5
  (Purchasing) of Title 2 (Administration) of the Huntington Park Municipal Code to
  add sections establishing financial due diligence standards prior to entering into city
  contracts and awarding public benefits; and

  2. Schedule second reading and adoption of said Ordinance for the October 27, 2026
  City Council meeting.

COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT

4.  CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL OF AN INTERIM URGENCY ORDINANCE
  IMPOSING A TEMPORARY MORATORIUM PROHIBITING APPROVAL AND
  ACCEPTANCE OF NEW DATA CENTER LAND USE APPLICATIONS PURSUANT
  TO GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 65858

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT THE CITY COUNCIL:

  1. Determine that Urgency Ordinance No. 2026-XX is categorically exempt from the
  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to State CEQA Guidelines
  Section 15061 (b)(3) (Common Sense Exemption); and

  2. Introduce by title only, and waive further reading of, Urgency Ordinance No. 2026-
  XX imposing a 45-day moratorium prohibiting approval and acceptance of new Data
  Center land use applications.

  END OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING AGENDA
  October 13, 2026  Page 7 of 6
   PUBLIC HEARING

COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT

1.  CONSIDERATION OF THE CONTINUED SUSPENSION, REVOCATION, OR
  REINSTATEMENT OF THE CANNABIS BUSINESS PERMIT ISSUED TO ALL
  DONE MANAGEMENT GROUP / PACKS SOUTH LOS ANGELES

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT THE CITY COUNCIL:

  1. Conduct a public hearing regarding the summary suspension of the cannabis
  business permit issued to All Done Management Group / Packs South Los Angeles;

  2. Receive and consider testimony, evidence, and arguments presented by the
  permittee, City staff, and interested parties; and

  3. Determine whether to continue the suspension, revoke the cannabis business
  permit, or terminate the suspension and reinstate the permit pursuant to Huntington
  Park Municipal Code (HPMC) Section 3-1.2408(d).

  END OF PUBLIC HEARING

  REPORTS AND INFORMATIONAL ITEMS

PUBLIC WORKS

1.  CONSIDERATION AND ADOPTION OF THE UPDATED VEHICLE REPLACEMENT
  POLICY (2026)
  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT THE CITY COUNCIL:
  1. Approve and adopt the updated Vehicle Replacement Policy (2026) and
  2. Authorize the Public Works Director, Finance Director, and City Manager to issue
  administrative updates as needed.

PARKS AND RECREATION

2.  CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL OF LICENSE AGREEMENT WITH FARM
  HABIT FOR USAGE OF SALT LAKE PARK FOR EVENING FARMERS MARKET
  FROM 2027 - 2028

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT THE CITY COUNCIL:

  1. Approve license agreement with Strando Inc. (DBA Farm Habit) for usage of Salt
  Lake Park from 2027–2028 at the monthly payment rate that must meet or exceed
  $1,000 and is negotiable based on market performance, with the option to revisit
  fees; and

  2. Authorize City Manager to execute Agreement.

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING AGENDA
  October 13, 2026  Page 8 of 6
 POLICE

3.  CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL TO AWARD FRANCHISE AGREEMENTS FOR
  ROTATIONAL POLICE TOWING AND VEHICLE STORAGE SERVICES

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT THE CITY COUNCIL:

  1. Approve the selection of U.S. Tow, Seventh Street Garage, Inc., and Mr. C’s
  Towing to participate in the City’s rotational Police Towing and Vehicle Storage
  Services program for an initial term of three (3) years, with options for two (2)
  additional one-year extensions at the City’s discretion, subject to satisfaction of all
  remaining requirements established by the RFP and before execution of the
  agreements and commencement of services; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager to finalize and execute a Franchise Agreement with
  each selected provider, subject to approval as to form.

CITY CLERK

4.  UPDATE REGARDING COMMISSION VACANCIES REQUIRING COUNCIL
  MEMBER ACTION

  IT IS RECOMMENDED THAT CITY COUNCIL:

  1. Receive an update regarding eleven (11) commission vacancies and provide an
  opportunity for Councilmembers Macias, Martinez, Sanabria, Martiz, and Flores to
  identify prospective appointees to fill their respective vacancies.

  END OF REPORTS AND INFORMATIONAL ITEMS

DEPARTMENTAL REPORTS

COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS

  Council Member Nancy Martiz
  Council Member Karina Macias
  Council Member Arturo Flores
  Vice Mayor Jonathan A. Sanabria
  Mayor Eduardo “Eddie” Martinez

ADJOURNMENT

The City of Huntington Park City Council will adjourn this meeting. The next Regular City
Council Meeting is scheduled for Tuesday, October 27, 2026, at Raul Perez Park 6208
Alameda Street, Huntington Park, 90255.
